The compiled reader confirms the pattern: in all ten sections the text block is at index 0 and every molecule and image block follows it. A figure therefore never sits beside the sentence it illustrates - the glycine cation, zwitterion, and anion are roughly 5,500 characters downstream of the sentence that introduces them.
findings.learner_impact: A reader who wants to check a structure against a claim has to leave the paragraph, scroll past the rest of the section, find the right figure among five to seven visually similar ones with no numbering to match against, and scroll back. That cost falls hardest on exactly the passages that most need a picture, and it makes the good figure clusters (the glycine charge triad, Ala-Gly versus Gly-Ala) far less useful than their content deserves.
findings.evidence: Reader sections[].blocks[] ordering: every section is [text, molecule|image ..., links]. Text block lengths 5415, 5852, 5592, 5781, 6239, 6146, 6970, 5964, 7111, 8699 characters. Regex sweep of all ten markdown blocks for figure references returned no hits.
findings.recommended_outcome: No figure in the chapter is anchored to the sentence it supports, and there is no numbering to bridge the gap. The need is for the reader to be able to connect a specific claim to the specific figure that shows it without hunting.

location.anchor_text: Four dipeptides result — Ala-Gly, Gly-Ala, Ala-Ala, and Gly-Gly

findings.observation: The reader fills 61 figure slots from 39 unique assets, so 22 slots (36 percent) are repeats, and the repeats carry their original captions into contexts that do not match. mol-glycine and mol-l-alanine each appear in five different sections, always captioned 'the one achiral standard amino acid' and 'the smallest chiral amino acid'. In the peptide-synthesis section, those two recycled classification figures open the section while the four scrambled dipeptides that ARE the section's opening problem (Ala-Gly, Gly-Ala, Ala-Ala, Gly-Gly) are represented by one of the four. In the synthesis section, glycine, alanine, and phenylalanine appear as route products with captions that say nothing about which route makes them or what aldehyde they came from.
findings.learner_impact: A repeated figure with a stale caption trains the reader to skip figures, which then costs them at the figures that do matter. It also actively fails the section it sits in: a learner scanning the peptide-synthesis section for 'the four dipeptides' finds one of them and two unrelated amino acids, and a learner scanning the synthesis section for the Strecker carbon-count trap finds a product with no starting material.
findings.evidence: Asset reuse across reader sections: mol-glycine 5, mol-l-alanine 5, mol-l-lysine 4, mol-l-cysteine 3, mol-l-proline 3, mol-l-histidine 2, mol-ala-gly-dipeptide 2, pdb-insulin-disulfides 2. nugget-peptide-synthesis figure order: mol-glycine, mol-l-alanine, mol-boc-glycine, mol-fmoc-glycine, mol-dcc, mol-ala-gly-dipeptide.
findings.recommended_outcome: Several figure slots are spent restating structures the reader has already seen, under captions written for a different section, while the comparison the section actually turns on is not shown. The need is for reused figures to either earn the new context (new caption, new thing to notice) or give up the slot.

location.anchor_text: with the molecule oriented so the hydrogen points away, the remaining three read counterclockwise

findings.observation: The stereochemistry section's procedure depends on two things the figures do not show. First, the alpha hydrogen: glycine carries show_hydrogens true, but every chiral amino acid in this section (mol-l-alanine, mol-l-serine, mol-l-cysteine, mol-l-valine, mol-l-threonine, mol-l-isoleucine) has no rdkit_options at all, so the hydrogen the CIP rule tells the reader to point away is implicit and invisible. Second, no asset requests CIP or stereo annotations, so the prose results 'L-Threonine is (2S,3R)' and 'L-isoleucine is (2S,3S)' cannot be checked against the drawing - the reader sees two wedge/dash centres with no indication of which is C2 and which is C3, or which descriptor belongs to which.
findings.learner_impact: A learner trying to execute the priority assignment on the figure has to supply the missing hydrogen themselves and guess its position, which is the step where the descriptor flips if you get it wrong. For threonine and isoleucine the two-descriptor result is simply unverifiable from the picture, so the figure cannot be used to check understanding - it can only be taken on trust.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json: only mol-glycine, mol-glycine-cation, mol-glycine-zwitterion, mol-glycine-anion, and mol-strecker-aminonitrile set rdkit_options; all five set show_hydrogens true and nothing else. No asset in the package sets annotation_font_scale or any CIP-label option. Prose: 'L-Threonine is (2S,3R) and L-isoleucine is (2S,3S)'.
findings.recommended_outcome: In the one section whose method is an atom-by-atom priority walk, the atom that anchors the walk is not drawn and the descriptors are not attached to the centres they describe. The need is for the stereocentre and its hydrogen to be inspectable on the figure the reader is asked to reason from.

location.anchor_text: Put L-serine and L-cysteine side by side with their carboxyl groups up and their hydrogens pointing back

findings.observation: The section's most important payoff - that L-serine (S) and L-cysteine (R) have the identical three-dimensional arrangement and only the naming rule differs - is delivered as an instruction to the reader to imagine two molecules in a shared orientation. The chapter supplies mol-l-serine and mol-l-cysteine as two independently laid-out 2D depictions separated by two other figures (cysteine is fourth in the section, serine third), with no shared orientation, no matched atom positions, and no priority numbering. The comparison the sentence asks the reader to perform is therefore not supported by the figures it sits next to. Separately, the section describes the Fischer convention in full ('carbon chain vertical, the carboxyl group at the top, the side chain at the bottom, horizontal bonds point toward the viewer') and no Fischer projection appears anywhere in the chapter, though ch26-build-l-alanine-fischer then asks the student to build one.
findings.learner_impact: The R/S-does-not-mean-shape lesson is the section's stated 'cleanest illustration in the course', and it lands only if the two structures are seen to be superimposable except at the sulfur. Two arbitrarily oriented depictions invite the opposite conclusion - that because the drawings look different, the molecules are arranged differently, which is precisely the misconception the passage exists to kill.
findings.evidence: Reader nugget-amino-acid-stereochemistry figure order: mol-glycine, mol-l-alanine, mol-l-serine, mol-l-cysteine, mol-l-valine, mol-l-threonine, mol-l-isoleucine. question-set.json ch26-build-l-alanine-fischer student_config uses fixed_top/fixed_bottom/substituent_options with no worked Fischer figure preceding it in the reader.
findings.recommended_outcome: The learner is told to compare two structures in a matched orientation and is given two unmatched drawings two positions apart. The need is for the sameness of the spatial arrangement, and the single point where the priority order differs, to be directly visible; and for the Fischer convention to be seen once before it is assessed.

location.anchor_text: A catalyst lowers ΔG‡ and leaves ΔG° alone.

findings.observation: The catalysis argument is an energy-profile argument made without an energy profile: an alternative pathway whose highest point is lower, unchanged reactant and product free energies, therefore unchanged equilibrium constant, both rate constants raised by the same factor because both directions cross the same lowered barrier, and separately the transition-state-stabilisation claim that binding energy must be released at the barrier top rather than in the enzyme-substrate well. There is no reaction coordinate diagram in this section or anywhere in the chapter.
findings.learner_impact: The most common misconception in this material - that a catalyst shifts the equilibrium - is a misreading of a picture the learner has never been shown. The distinction between a deep substrate well (which slows the reaction) and a lowered barrier is a difference in the shape of a curve, and describing that difference in sentences asks the reader to draw the curve themselves in order to see the point.
findings.evidence: nugget-enzymes-and-catalysis prose: 'It offers an alternative pathway whose highest point is lower than that of the uncatalysed path' and 'if it were, the enzyme would simply create a deep thermodynamic well and slow the reaction down'. No diagram block exists in the chapter.
findings.recommended_outcome: The learner is given an argument about the shape of an energy profile with no profile to look at. The need is for the catalysed-versus-uncatalysed barrier comparison, and the enzyme-substrate well versus transition-state well distinction, to be visible.

location.anchor_text: Histidine is the workhorse here, because the imidazole pKa near 6 puts both its protonated and neutral forms in play at physiological pH.

findings.observation: The three molecule figures in the enzyme section are mol-l-cysteine, mol-l-lysine, and mol-l-glutamine, all reused free amino acids carrying their classification-section captions. The residue the section singles out by name as the workhorse of general acid-base catalysis - histidine - is not among them, and neither are Glu35, Asp52, or the serine of the serine proteases, all of which the text names and reasons about. Glutamine, which appears in the section only in a closing list of what side chains offer, gets a figure; histidine, which gets a whole paragraph and drives the lysozyme and citrate synthase discussions, does not.
findings.learner_impact: The figures point the reader's attention at the wrong residues. A learner using the figure set as a study cue would come away thinking cysteine, lysine, and glutamine are the catalytic residues to know, when the section's argument runs through histidine and the carboxylates.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json nugget-enzymes-and-catalysis asset_ids: pdb-lysozyme-fold, pdb-citrate-synthase, mol-l-cysteine, mol-l-lysine, mol-l-glutamine. mol-l-histidine is assigned to nugget-zwitterions and nugget-isoelectric-point only, despite its concept_slugs including enzymes-and-catalysis.
findings.recommended_outcome: The section's figures do not show the residues the section is about. The need is for the visual attention in this section to land on the catalytic side chains the prose actually reasons with, and for figures whose caption no longer matches their new job to be re-captioned or dropped.

location.anchor_text: Proteins built this way are globular and generally soluble — enzymes, transport proteins, antibodies.

findings.observation: The antibody schematic's stated learning goal is to make disulfide cross-linking and quaternary structure 'legible at a glance, before the atomic detail arrives', yet in the compiled reader it is placed last, after all four atomic ribbon renders, so the atomic detail arrives first. The prose of this section never discusses antibodies beyond a three-word appearance in a list of globular proteins, and the section's worked quaternary example is haemoglobin. The schematic therefore has no anchoring sentence and no ordering rationale where it currently sits.
findings.learner_impact: A simplified schematic placed after four ribbon diagrams reads as decoration rather than as scaffolding. Its potential value - a clean, colour-coded picture of four chains held by disulfides that the reader can carry into the harder renders - is lost by ordering, and a reader looking for the sentence it illustrates will not find one.
findings.evidence: Reader nugget-protein-structure-levels block order: text, 1MBN, 1EMA, 1HHO, 1ZNI, mol-l-proline, mol-cystine-disulfide, antibody clipart, external link. Asset clip-antibody-schematic learning_goal: 'The Y-shaped assembly that makes disulfide cross-linking and quaternary structure legible at a glance, before the atomic detail arrives.'
findings.recommended_outcome: A deliberately simplified figure is doing its work after the complex figures it was meant to prepare the reader for, against prose that never invokes it. The need is for the simple-to-complex ordering the asset itself declares, and for the figure to be tied to a claim in the text or removed.

location.anchor_text: Myoglobin, whose structure was the first ever determined for a protein, is about 75 percent helix, arranged as eight segments folded around a heme.

findings.observation: I inspected 1mbn_assembly-1.jpeg directly. It is a rainbow N-to-C spectrum ribbon: the colour encodes chain position, not helix identity, so the eight helical segments the caption and prose both count are not separable by eye, and the heme sits toward the top of the frame as small grey sticks rather than being enclosed by the fold as the alt text ('folded into a compact globule around a flat disc-shaped heme group') states. Nothing labels the heme, and nothing tells the reader what the colour ramp means. The same unexplained rainbow convention is used for 1EMA and 2LYZ while 1HHO and 5CSC use per-chain colouring, so the chapter's protein images teach two different, unstated colour languages.
findings.learner_impact: A reader who tries to verify 'eight segments' from the picture cannot, and a reader who does not know the rainbow convention may reasonably infer that colour marks different chains - which then makes myoglobin look like a multi-subunit protein in the very section that contrasts one-chain myoglobin with four-chain haemoglobin.
findings.evidence: Assets pdb-myoglobin-alpha-helix (1MBN, rainbow), pdb-gfp-beta-barrel (1EMA, rainbow), pdb-lysozyme-fold (2LYZ, rainbow) versus pdb-haemoglobin-quaternary (1HHO, four chain colours) and pdb-citrate-synthase (5CSC, two chain colours), all inspected from their cdn.rcsb.org URLs.
findings.recommended_outcome: The reader cannot tell what the colours mean, and the countable feature the caption names is not countable in the render. The need is for the colour convention to be stated and for the caption to claim only what the image actually lets a reader see.

findings.observation: Structure support in the question bank is inconsistent within the same chapter. ch26-identify-nonpolar-side-chain, ch26-select-polar-neutral-side-chains and ch26-sort-side-chain-classes attach structure_smiles to every option, so the student compares drawn side chains. ch26-rank-isoelectric-points, which asks for the same kind of side-chain reading, renders its four cards as text descriptions only ('L-Histidine, side chain CH₂ attached to an imidazole ring'), and ch26-aspartate-electrophoresis-reasoning asks the student to assign protonation states to three named groups with nothing drawn.
findings.learner_impact: A student who has been trained by the first three questions to read structures is abruptly asked to parse a prose formula instead, and to hold three ionisable groups on an undrawn molecule while assigning charges. The inconsistency is small per question but it removes the visual channel exactly where the reasoning is multi-step.
findings.evidence: question-set.json: ch26-identify-nonpolar-side-chain has 4 structure_smiles, ch26-select-polar-neutral-side-chains 6, ch26-sort-side-chain-classes 8; ch26-rank-isoelectric-points and ch26-aspartate-electrophoresis-reasoning have 0.
findings.recommended_outcome: The same reasoning is supported by structures in some questions and by prose formulas in others. The need is for the ranking and electrophoresis questions to give the student the side chains and ionisable groups to look at, as their siblings already do.

location.anchor_text: Three disulfide bonds hold the mature hormone together — two interchain links joining the A and B chains, plus one intrachain link that closes a small loop within the A chain itself.

findings.observation: pdb-insulin-disulfides is placed twice in the compiled reader - once in nugget-peptide-sequencing and once in nugget-protein-structure-levels - with byte-identical caption and alt text in both. Inspecting 1zni_assembly-1.jpeg confirms the disulfides are in fact drawn as yellow sticks, so the alt text is accurate, but the three bonds the prose asks the reader to distinguish (two interchain, one intrachain) are unlabelled small sticks and the molecule occupies only about half the frame against white space.
findings.learner_impact: The duplicate adds nothing on second encounter, and in both places the specific claim the reader is meant to verify - which bridge is interchain and which closes the loop within the A chain - is not distinguishable at the size and labelling provided.
findings.evidence: Reader blocks blk-lnn5q30b (nugget-peptide-sequencing) and blk-75jmbi3u (nugget-protein-structure-levels), identical url, alt_text and caption. Image inspected from https://cdn.rcsb.org/images/structures/1zni_assembly-1.jpeg.
findings.recommended_outcome: The same image appears twice saying the same thing, and in neither place supports the counting the prose asks for. The need is for one placement that lets the reader tell the three disulfides apart, or a caption that stops implying they can.

strengths: The glycine cation / zwitterion / anion triad (mol-glycine-cation, mol-glycine-zwitterion, mol-glycine-anion) is the best figure work in the chapter: three purpose-built species, each with show_hydrogens true so the moving proton is actually visible, differing in exactly the one feature the section is about. SUFFICIENT AS IS - no new asset needed here.

Ala-Gly versus Gly-Ala (mol-ala-gly-dipeptide, mol-gly-ala-dipeptide) is a genuinely earned pair: two constitutional isomers whose difference is only legible as a picture, supporting the claim that sequence direction makes a different substance. SUFFICIENT AS IS.

Boc-glycine versus Fmoc-glycine (mol-boc-glycine, mol-fmoc-glycine) is a real comparison - the fluorene versus tert-butyl contrast explains the acid/base orthogonality at a glance, and the comparison_matrix question that follows carries both structures. SUFFICIENT AS IS.

Legibility hygiene is good and should not be disturbed: show_hydrogens is set on exactly five assets, all of them small (glycine and its three charge states, 2-aminopropanenitrile), and never on tryptophan, DCC, Fmoc-glycine, cystine or any other heavy structure. No asset anywhere in the package sets annotation_font_scale, so there is no risk of a stereo label being drawn over the structure it labels.

pdb-haemoglobin-quaternary (1HHO) works as intended - four chains in four clearly distinct colours with four visible hemes makes quaternary structure immediately readable, and it is the right image for the teaching point. pdb-gfp-beta-barrel (1EMA) likewise shows the barrel and its constituent strands clearly. SUFFICIENT AS IS.

mol-cystine-disulfide is the right figure for the disulfide cross-link: it shows the S-S bond joining two complete residues, which is exactly what the primary-structure and sequencing arguments turn on.

The classification cluster in section 1 (glycine, alanine, serine, aspartic acid, lysine, proline) is not filler - six residues spanning nonpolar, polar-uncharged, acidic, basic, and the ring-closed exception, each doing distinct work against the five-family scheme.

Where questions do carry structures they carry them well: ch26-amide-resonance-arrow, ch26-locate-peptide-bond, ch26-peptide-bond-ledger and ch26-sequencing-plan-repair all supply molecule_smiles for Ala-Gly, so the arrow, the click target, and the bond ledger are performed on a visible structure rather than an imagined one. ch26-build-l-alanine-fischer gives the student an interactive Fischer projection to construct.
Reader compilation is faithful - every asset_id listed on every nugget in the topic package is present in the corresponding reader section, with no dropped figures.
open_questions: All three video briefs (video-zwitterion-titration, video-peptide-bond-formation, video-edman-cycle) are production_status deferred, so nothing in the chapter animates or sequences. Notably, none of the three covers the alpha-helix / beta-sheet geometry, which on this review is the largest told-not-shown gap in the chapter - was that omission deliberate?

I inferred figure placement from block order in the compiled reader (one text block, then all figures). If the reader UI reflows molecule and image blocks inline or into a side rail near referenced text, finding visual-008 weakens considerably - can someone confirm how sections[].blocks[] are laid out on screen?

Does the reader re-render or crop the cdn.rcsb.org assembly JPEGs, or are they shown at their native 500x500? Several (1ZNI in particular) carry substantial white space, which affects how large the relevant feature appears.

For visual-005 I used category figure-purpose, but the issue is really a figure that is chemically correct in isolation and misleading in the section it was placed in. If that pattern recurs across chapters, a distinct id such as figure-context-mismatch may be worth adding to the schema.

mol-l-histidine lists enzymes-and-catalysis among its concept_slugs but is not attached to nugget-enzymes-and-catalysis (see visual-013) - is that an authoring oversight or a deliberate placement decision?

executive_summary: Chemically this is the cleanest chapter reviewed in the series: the instructor persona machine-verified all 32 asset SMILES and all 42 distinct structures inside questions, confirmed every stereodescriptor, every net formal charge, every pI recomputation and all 40 answer keys, and found no D residue anywhere — the failure mode this package type is most prone to. Both of its blockers are single clauses: a figure description that generalises the (S) result to 'every L-amino acid whose side chain begins with carbon' (cysteine's does, and it is R), and an Edman step that adds the amine across C=S rather than C=N. Readiness is nevertheless blocked, and by accessibility rather than chemistry: all 40 accessible_descriptions are authored well and rendered nowhere, both hotspot items name atoms only as 'C atom 4', and structure_scaffold still offers no non-drawing response path. Those are platform tickets already open on ch1, 11, 15-19, 23 and 25. The dominant chapter-level theme, reached independently by three personas, is that this chapter reasons from pictures it never shows: a titration curve, an energy profile, residue-scale helix and sheet geometry, and the planar peptide unit with its phi/psi hinges. All four are asserted in prose and then assessed. Separately, an orchestrator check found the asset-to-nugget links inconsistent in both directions, which is why histidine — the residue the enzyme section argues from — renders nowhere in that section.
consensus_strengths: Zero wrong structures and zero wrong answer keys across 40 questions and 74 distinct SMILES, machine-verified: all 18 chiral L-amino acids (S), cysteine (R), threonine (2S,3R), isoleucine (2S,3S), both cystine halves (R), and every net formal charge matching its label.

Every claim made about the six Protein Data Bank entries checks out against RCSB, including that 1ZNI assembly 1 is the A+B heterodimer the alt text describes and 1HHO assembly 1 is the alpha-2 beta-2 tetramer.
Wrong-answer explanations consistently name the discriminating idea rather than scolding, and the $missing matchers also tell a student why an option they omitted belonged.

All 39 assets carry both alt_text and a long_description that teaches the figure, and the comparison pairs are differentiated in exactly the respect the comparison turns on — the strongest authored accessibility content in the pipeline so far.
No accessibility answer leaks in any of the 40 accessible_descriptions, confirmed by both the automated guard and the accessibility persona reading them.
The cysteine R/S passage, the zwitterion section's failed-prediction opening, and the isoelectric-point section's four worked cases are singled out by multiple personas as genuinely good teaching.

Legibility hygiene is clean: show_hydrogens is set on exactly five small molecules and never on a large one, and no asset sets annotation_font_scale, so the stereo-label burial that affected ch14 and ch18 cannot occur here.

ranked_recommendations.title: L-alanine figure states the exact rule cysteine breaks
ranked_recommendations.need: A figure description generalises the (S) result to 'every L-amino acid whose side chain begins with carbon'. Cysteine's side chain begins with carbon and is (R) — the description asserts, exceptionlessly, the rule the next section exists to refute.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: A single false clause in one long_description. Deleting or qualifying it fully removes the error; the structure itself is correct and needs no change.

ranked_recommendations.title: Edman walkthrough adds the amine across the wrong double bond
ranked_recommendations.need: Step 2 instructs the student to add the N-terminal amine across the C=S bond of phenyl isothiocyanate. The addition is across C=N; the C=S survives into the product, as step 3 of the same walkthrough correctly describes.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: One clause in one step, and the walkthrough already contradicts itself one step later — correcting the clause makes the activity self-consistent without touching its structure.

ranked_recommendations.title: Question accessible_descriptions reach no student surface
ranked_recommendations.need: All 40 questions carry a well-written accessible_description and no delivery surface renders it, so the chapter's entire non-visual stimulus-equivalence strategy is inert.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Authoring is already correct and complete; the gap is renderer-side. Recorded as a platform ticket rather than re-authored, because no chapter-level edit can fix it. Previously proved on ch16 and open on ch19.

ranked_recommendations.title: Hotspot atoms are named only by RDKit index
ranked_recommendations.need: Both hotspot items give a screen-reader user buttons named 'C atom 4' over an image whose alt is 'Structure for this question'. 'Click the two atoms joined by the peptide bond' is then unanswerable except by guessing.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The curved_arrow items in the same chapter already carry chemically named sites, so the fix is a configuration pattern the platform supports. Same class as the ch25 hotspot finding.

ranked_recommendations.title: structure_scaffold offers no non-drawing response path
ranked_recommendations.need: Both structure_scaffold items are a blank Ketcher canvas with no SMILES, name, or assemble-from-fragments alternative. The platform registry itself records keyboard_complete=False.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: A standing platform ticket (open on ch1, 11, 15-19, 23, 25). No chapter edit closes it; the least-complex chapter-level mitigation is to ensure each affected concept is also assessed by a non-drawing type, which it already is.

ranked_recommendations.title: Glycine carries two different pKa pairs across prose and questions
ranked_recommendations.need: The zwitterion section uses 2.34 / 9.60 and runs a full Henderson-Hasselbalch calculation on them; the matching question states 2.35 / 9.78 with pI 6.06. Both pairs are real literature values, but a student who memorises the reading does not recognise the numbers in the question.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Internal consistency, not correctness. Aligning the questions to the prose set is far fewer edits than re-deriving the section's worked Henderson-Hasselbalch arithmetic, and leaves the derivations the student can check intact.

ranked_recommendations.title: Prose teaches five side-chain families; the questions grade four
ranked_recommendations.need: The prose names an aromatic family and files tyrosine there; the sort question offers four bins with no aromatic one, and the multi-select keys tyrosine as polar-uncharged. A student who learned the prose scheme meets a question with no box for their answer.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The two schemes are both defensible; what is not defensible is switching silently. Naming the relationship where the student meets the four-bin scheme is smaller and less disruptive than re-authoring either the prose taxonomy or two questions.

ranked_recommendations.title: The compiler drops every long_description on the way to the reader
ranked_recommendations.need: All 39 assets carry a long_description that teaches the figure; the compiled reader contains zero occurrences of the field, so image blocks arrive with alt text only.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: A three-line change in the reader chapter builder passes authored content that already exists through to the surface that needs it — strictly smaller than re-authoring alt text to carry the long description's load.

ranked_recommendations.title: The isoelectric-point section reasons from a titration curve it never shows
ranked_recommendations.need: The section opens by telling the student to read a titration curve backwards, describes its plateaus and steep regions, and locates pI inside one — with no curve anywhere in the chapter.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Three personas reached this independently and it is the chapter's most-cited gap. A description cannot substitute: the skill being taught is reading a graph. Blocked on there being no topic-package asset kind that renders a titration curve, so it is recorded as a need rather than built here.

ranked_recommendations.title: The catalysis argument is an energy-profile argument with no energy profile
ranked_recommendations.need: The claim that a catalyst lowers the barrier and leaves the endpoints alone is asserted three times, is the discriminator in the keyed multi-select, and the question's own first hint tells the student to draw the profile the chapter never showed them.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The misconception being targeted is a misreading of a picture the learner has never seen. The reaction_coordinate asset kind exists and could carry this, but the science-review rule restricts those diagrams to clean one- or two-step profiles; a catalysed-versus-uncatalysed comparison qualifies and should be authored deliberately rather than improvised mid-review.

ranked_recommendations.title: Helix and sheet geometry is asserted, assessed, and never shown at residue scale
ranked_recommendations.need: The i+4-to-i hydrogen bond, 3.6 residues per turn, side chains 100 degrees apart, and parallel-versus-antiparallel strand direction are carried by sentences; the section's five images are whole-protein ribbons in which no hydrogen bond or side chain is resolvable. A twelve-cell matrix then grades exactly those details.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The whole-protein renders are the right figures for tertiary and quaternary structure and should stay; what is missing is a complementary residue-scale view. That is an addition, not a replacement.

ranked_recommendations.title: The planar peptide unit, phi/psi, and cis/trans are described but never drawn
ranked_recommendations.need: Six named coplanar atoms, the rigid-plate-and-hinge picture of the backbone, the trans-versus-cis contrast, and the Ramachandran result are all words; the section's figures are flat 2D structures that cannot show a plane or a torsion.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Later sections depend on this picture, so it is scaffolding rather than decoration. A single annotated backbone segment covers the plate, both torsions, and the trans/cis contrast at once.

ranked_recommendations.title: The chapter's flagship result — cysteine is (R) — is never assessed
ranked_recommendations.need: The stereochemistry concept's second objective is accounting for cysteine's descriptor, and the section is titled for it. Both questions on that concept are Fischer builds; no question in the bank asks about the CIP flip, threonine, or isoleucine.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The material and the verified structures already exist; a single select item plus its variant closes the objective-alignment gap without disturbing the bank's shape.

ranked_recommendations.title: The error the chapter calls the most common is never assessable
ranked_recommendations.need: The Strecker carbon-count trap is named in the prose as 'the single most common error on Strecker problems' and exercised only in a practice check that no reader surface renders. No question tests it.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: A chapter that names its own most common error should give the student one place to make it and be corrected. One item, using structures already verified.

ranked_recommendations.title: Two enzyme figure captions promise features their renders do not contain
ranked_recommendations.need: The lysozyme alt text asserts 'a pronounced groove running across one face' and citrate synthase 'a deep interior cavity'; both renders are unlabelled apo ribbons with no bound substrate in which neither feature is locatable.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Either the image changes or the claim does. Re-rendering with a bound ligand and highlighted residues is out of scope for a review pass, and the caption is the thing that is actually false — so correct the caption and alt text to claim only what the render shows.

ranked_recommendations.title: Neutral free-base structures sit inside the charge-ladder section
ranked_recommendations.need: Aspartic acid, lysine, histidine and glutamic acid render in the isoelectric-point section drawn as uncharged amines with intact COOH — species that exist at no pH — beside prose that calls exactly that depiction 'a convenient fiction'.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The structures are chemically correct and belong where they were authored (the classification section). The defect is placement, so the least-complex fix is to correct the section's figure list rather than redraw anything.

ranked_recommendations.title: Asset-to-nugget links disagree in both directions
ranked_recommendations.need: An orchestrator link check (orchestrator-002) found fourteen assets naming a nugget whose asset_ids does not list them, so those placements never render — histidine, the residue the enzyme section argues from, appears nowhere in that section. Sixteen more render in sections their own metadata does not claim, which is what carries stale captions into new contexts.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Pure metadata reconciliation. It simultaneously fixes the missing-histidine finding, the stale-caption finding, and the misplaced free-base figures, so it is the single highest-leverage edit in the set.

ranked_recommendations.title: Only the expanded tier reaches the reader surface
ranked_recommendations.need: All three text tiers compile into the reader chapter as _detail_texts, but the reader block renderer reads only content.markdown, so a struggling student gets ten unbroken 5,000-8,700 character essays with no lighter path.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The data is present and one renderer (the Deck Creator textbook view) already switches on it; the reader simply does not. A renderer change, recorded as a platform ticket. Separately the terse tiers as written are compression rather than simplification, which is an authoring note.

ranked_recommendations.title: No practice_check or video reaches the reader
ranked_recommendations.need: All ten nuggets carry a practice_check with a worked answer and none appears in the reader; all three video briefs are deferred, so nothing in the chapter checks understanding or moves.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The material is authored; the reader has no block type for it. Platform ticket, already open from ch19. The video deferral is separately recorded in the coherence pass.

ranked_recommendations.title: Two graded facts are never taught
ranked_recommendations.need: The Boc/Fmoc matrix grades a UV-absorbance row, and the chymotrypsin item keys the oxyanion hole; neither appears in any depth tier of the chapter.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Both are one clause of chemistry each, genuinely worth teaching and already implied by the surrounding text — cheaper and more useful than deleting a matrix row and an option.

ranked_recommendations.title: Protease specificities are stated without their proline exceptions
ranked_recommendations.need: Trypsin, chymotrypsin and cyanogen bromide are given as exceptionless rules; all three fail before proline, and CNBr converts methionine to a homoserine lactone. The chapter has just taught why proline behaves differently.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: A qualifier sentence, and it pays off a distinction the chapter already established.

ranked_recommendations.title: Three small factual and framing slips in the prose
ranked_recommendations.need: The 40 percent double-bond figure is presented as following from the bond length (interpolation gives 75 percent); pyruvic acid is offered as a rejected Strecker substrate when it is not an aldehyde at all; and phi/psi rotation is called 'entirely free' one sentence before the Ramachandran plot, which exists because it is not.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Three independent single-clause corrections; each is verifiably wrong as written and cheap to fix.

ranked_recommendations.title: RCSB credit is not rendered for the six protein figures
ranked_recommendations.need: The protein image blocks record RCSB provenance but carry no content.attribution, and the reader renders only content.attribution — so the credit reaches no one, visually or non-visually. The NIAID schematic does surface its credit.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: One line in the reader chapter builder, mirroring what the clipart branch already does.

ranked_recommendations.title: Assessment lets two targeted misconceptions pass undetected
ranked_recommendations.need: The pI ranking can be answered perfectly by ranking side-chain acidity — the exact misconception the concept's trouble_spots name — and no feedback distinguishes the two. The Fischer item's last hint defers to L-glyceraldehyde, which the chapter never draws or configures.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Feedback and hint text edits; the questions themselves are sound and their keys are correct.

ranked_recommendations.title: Two asserted numbers cannot be reproduced from any stated rule
ranked_recommendations.need: The 10^7.5 internal proton-transfer constant needs the rule that K = 10^(pKa difference), and the '15 kcal/mol' figure needs the ~1.36 kcal/mol per power of ten conversion; neither rule appears anywhere in the chapter.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Half a sentence each. The section already models careful arithmetic elsewhere, which is what makes these two stand out as unexplained.

ranked_recommendations.title: Reader figures are hot-linked with no offline or failure fallback
ranked_recommendations.need: Six RCSB images and the clipart proxy are remote URLs in an installable offline PWA, with no fallbackSrc; offline or CDN-blocked readers get a broken image where the structure should be.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Platform ticket — caching or fallback belongs to the reader shell, not the chapter. Mitigated in the meantime because the prose carries the same chemistry.

ranked_recommendations.title: Figures are appended after the prose rather than anchored to it
ranked_recommendations.need: Every section is one long text block followed by all its figures, and the prose never refers to a figure, so no figure sits beside the sentence it illustrates.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Structural to the compiler's one-text-block-per-nugget model; a full fix is a pipeline change. Recorded as a need, with the figure-placement corrections in rec-016 and rec-017 taking the sharpest edge off it.

ranked_recommendations.title: Two figure titles and one duplicate placement mislead
ranked_recommendations.need: The aspartate dianion title points at 'both carboxyls deprotonated', which already describes the -1 monoanion; the myoglobin caption asks the reader to count eight helices in a rainbow render where they are not separable; the insulin image appears twice with identical caption and alt text.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Caption and metadata edits, each independently verifiable.

ranked_recommendations.title: Notation and heading polish in the accessibility channel
ranked_recommendations.need: Six alt texts use ASCII 'CH2' where the prose uses CH₂; molecule cards announce their description twice; image blocks emit no heading and no programmatic caption association; the hotspot and curved-arrow level-3 hints state the answer outright.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Small independent edits; the hint-leak items matter most because they hit the students who most need hints.

ranked_recommendations.title: Bare chapter-number cross-references collide with the textbook mappings
ranked_recommendations.need: The prose points back with 'Chapter 21', 'Chapter 11', 'Chapter 25' and 'Chapter 23'. These are McMurry numbers, but this same package maps to Klein chapter 25 and McMurry Fundamentals chapter 23 — so a Klein student reading 'chemistry taken directly from Chapter 25' is pointed at the chapter they are currently in.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Naming the topic instead of the number makes the reference resolve for every mapped book, and it is a smaller change than carrying per-textbook numbering through the prose.

ranked_recommendations.title: Turning figures off deletes them rather than collapsing them to text
ranked_recommendations.need: The reader's 'Structures and diagrams' preference removes all 40 figure blocks together with their alt text and captions, so a learner who turns figures off for cognitive load or bandwidth is left with no record that a figure existed.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The control reads as a display preference and behaves as content deletion. Collapsing to the description is the behaviour the label already implies. Platform ticket — it affects every chapter.

ranked_recommendations.title: The chapter's only textbook link is the generic landing page
ranked_recommendations.need: The compiled reader carries one mcmurry_link, pointing at '26-why-this-chapter', which the production skill's own rule forbids as a reading target.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: A false alarm at chapter level with a real cause behind it: the three specific OpenStax section links for this chapter live in [internal source reference — not in this repo] and render in the reader's Additional Reading panel, not in the compiled chapter JSON. The generic link is hardcoded in the reader chapter builder and affects every chapter, so it is a pipeline note rather than a ch26 correction.

disagreements.topic: Whether the whole-protein PDB renders are the right figures for the secondary-structure section

positions.Accessibility Persona: Rates the protein figure descriptions as the strongest authored accessibility content in the pipeline, differentiated in exactly the respects the comparisons turn on, and raises no objection to the figures themselves.
positions.Learner with Visual Preference: Calls the same five images unable to resolve a single hydrogen bond, residue index, strand direction or side-chain face, and therefore incapable of showing what the section asserts and the matrix question grades.

disagreements.resolution: Both are right about different things and neither cancels the other. The descriptions are excellent AS DESCRIPTIONS OF THOSE IMAGES; the images are the wrong scale for the residue-level claims. Resolved by keeping every render and every description unchanged and recording the need for a complementary residue-scale figure (rec-011) — an addition, not a replacement. Nothing here justifies removing a figure the accessibility review rates highly.

disagreements.topic: Severity of the missing titration curve

positions.Organic Chemistry Instructor: high — the section is constructed entirely around a curve that does not exist.
positions.Struggling Student: high — cannot visualise a plateau from a sentence, so falls back on memorising 'average two pKa values', the exact surface strategy the section says it wants to prevent.
positions.Learner with Visual Preference: medium — notes there is no block type in the compiled reader capable of carrying a plot at all.

disagreements.resolution: Kept at high, the strongest severity of the three, per the reconciliation rule. The visual persona's lower rating rests on the absence of a rendering path, which is an argument about feasibility rather than about learner impact — and feasibility is the orchestrator's problem, not a reason to downgrade the need.
